column1: # Which screens each Maestro flow passes through. One row per top-level flow (the ids `runMaestroFlows.sh plan`
# prints), a TAB, then a comma-separated list of screens (a module of mobile/src/screens that the navigator or the
# auth gate registers). HomeScreen is added to every flow by the selector, because every flow signs in through Home.
# A row must name EVERY screen the flow reaches, the ones it only passes through included. A screen missing from a
# row is a screen whose change does not run that flow. Running too many is only slow; running too few is the
# failure the selector exists to avoid. When unsure, list more screens.
# SEEDED AT THE GRAIN OF THE RUNNER'S VERTICALS (auth, home, recipes, discovery, collections), plus every screen for
# the shell flows that walk the tab bar. That is coarse on purpose: nothing here has been observed on a device, and
# a flow cannot be read for the screens it reaches the way a Playwright spec can. Narrow a row only after watching
# THE SCREEN RECORDER CHECKS THIS FILE. A local lane run (`npm run test:e2e:android`, `test:e2e:ios`) uses a test build
# that logs each screen it shows (`mobile/src/screenTrace`); after the run, `@kitchensink/e2e-plan/recordedScreens` fails
# the run when a flow showed a screen its combined row lacks (add it), or passed having recorded nothing. It also prints
# rows WIDER than what a passed flow showed. Narrow a row only from several observed runs: one run takes one branch of a
# `when:`. Adding a screen to a row is always safe; the recorder never narrows by itself.
# A SUB-FLOW may have a row too (the two sign-in flows do): its screens belong to every top-level flow that runs it,
# through the flow graph, so a flow's own row lists only what the flow adds.
# The guard (tests/e2eScreenRegistry.integration.test.ts) fails when a top-level flow has no row, a row names no
# flow or sub-flow, or a row names a screen that does not exist.
